title: Private task never planned on Dahl (public)
scenario: Provider table: dahl (public, priority 0), groq (private), ollama (local). A private task asks for a chain.
expected: Chain is exactly [ollama, groq]; dahl absent.

title: Only Dahl available: private task fails closed
scenario: The only available provider is public Dahl; every private provider is disabled or keyless. A private task is planned.
expected: plan() raises RouteError; the lane is never widened to public.

title: Public task never gets a private provider
scenario: A public (test-agent) task with groq private at priority 0 and dahl public at 50.
expected: Chain is exactly [dahl].

title: Paid or unknown-lane provider never used
scenario: Private lane: a paid private provider at priority 0, a provider with lane 'cloud', and one free private provider.
expected: Chain is exactly [free]; paid and unknown-lane providers excluded.

title: Missing key file skipped, present key used
scenario: Two private providers: one whose key file does not exist, one whose key file is present.
expected: Chain is exactly [haskey]; no exception for the missing key.

title: Unknown task lane refused
scenario: A task arrives with lane 'owner' (not private/public) and every provider available.
expected: plan() raises RouteError (no default lane is assumed).

title: Priority order, ties broken local-first then config order
scenario: Private lane: b (private, 10), a (private, 10), loc (local, 10), slow (local, 90), purpose filter 'code' with one provider lacking it.
expected: Chain is exactly [loc, b, a, slow]; 'nocode' excluded by purpose.

title: Route explanation codes are truthful
scenario: explain() for a private 20k-token request: a small provider (8k), a resting one, dahl public, a paid one, and the owner-preferred one.
expected: small has CONTEXT_TOO_SMALL, resting has RESTING_AFTER_ERRORS, dahl LANE_MISMATCH, paid PAID_REFUSED; chosen is the preferred 'big'.

title: Gateway call: scrub, lane, private key block
scenario: gateway.call() on a private task with a GitHub token in the prompt; Dahl (public) is priority 0, the first private provider answers 500. Then a prompt with a PEM private key.
expected: Answer from the 2nd private provider; Dahl gets 0 requests; the token never leaves (sent text has [REDACTED]); the private-key prompt raises RouteError with 0 further requests; audit has no token.

title: Free-model guard refuses a paid model before sending
scenario: An OpenRouter-style provider configured with a paid model but pattern ':free$', followed by a free provider.
expected: The guarded provider gets 0 requests; the next provider answers; a model_refused audit row exists.

title: Empty reply and unreachable provider fall through
scenario: Chain: a provider answering with empty content, one with nothing listening, then a good one. Second call without the good one.
expected: First call returns the good answer; second raises RouteError 'all providers failed'; audit classes include ValueError and URLError.

title: Provider timeout honoured in gateway.call
scenario: First provider hangs 3 s with timeout_s=1; second answers immediately.
expected: Second provider's answer within 2.5 s total.

title: Token estimate close to measured ratio
scenario: A 24k-character prose request (and the same with a 4k-char tool schema).
expected: estimate/(chars/4.66) between 1.0 and 1.3 (safe over-estimate, not wildly off); tool schema adds >= 900 tokens; empty request >= 1.

title: Provider refusals classified
scenario: Refusals: 413; 400 'maximum context length'; 400 'invalid tool'; 429 'rate limit'; 429 'Request too large ... tokens per minute'; 500; 401.
expected: Classes: too_large, too_large, other, rate_limited, too_large, other, other.

cases: This model's maximum context length is 8192
Request too large for model in organization on tokens per min

title: Rate-limit rest times
scenario: Retry-After '20'; Retry-After '999999'; Retry-After 'soon' with no text; daily quota text; nothing.

title: Fit and answer-budget arithmetic
scenario: An 8000 total-token provider and a 120k input provider; requests of 6000/7500/100k/130k tokens.
expected: 8000-total fits 6000 not 7500, answer budget 2000 for 6000 in; 120k fits 100k not 130k; lane context 120000; small lane reported as 64000.

title: Summary calls detected and checked
scenario: A Hermes compression call (and the same with tools); summary replies cut at the cap, too short, complete, malformed.
expected: Detected only without tools; cut->truncated, short->empty, complete ok, malformed->no choices.

title: Proxy: primary success relayed, key added
scenario: An agent call through the real llm_proxy to a mock primary.
expected: HTTP 200 with the provider body unchanged; the provider got the proxy's key and configured model; neither key nor agent token in the audit; < 500 ms.

title: Proxy: 429 falls back and the primary rests
scenario: Primary answers 429 with Retry-After 20 on the first call; a same-lane fallback answers. A second call inside 20 s, a third after.
expected: Calls 1-2 answered by the fallback, primary asked once during its rest; after 21 s the primary answers again.

title: Proxy: every provider rate limited
scenario: The only provider of the public lane answers 429 Retry-After 45; the agent calls twice.
expected: Both calls get 429 with Retry-After <= 45; the second is answered without asking the provider again.

title: Proxy: provider timeout falls back
scenario: Primary hangs 3 s with timeout_s=1; fallback answers.
expected: HTTP 200 from the fallback within 2.5 s; the timeout is audited for the primary.

title: Proxy: malformed JSON summary rejected
scenario: A context-compression call; the primary answers 200 with HTML/invalid JSON; the fallback returns a 400-char summary.
expected: HTTP 200 with the fallback's summary; the broken body is never passed on.

title: Proxy: malformed normal reply does not break it
scenario: A normal call whose provider returns invalid JSON, then a normal call.
expected: The bytes are relayed as-is (proxy never parses normal replies) and the next call gets HTTP 200.

title: Proxy: 401 key failure, echoing error page
scenario: The primary rejects its key with 401 and echoes the Authorization header in its error body; a fallback exists. Then the bad provider alone.
expected: With fallback: HTTP 200. Alone: HTTP 502 mentioning 401. No configured key appears in either reply or the audit.

title: Proxy: three keys never leak
scenario: Three providers with distinct synthetic keys: 429, 500, success, streaming, then all failing.
expected: No key in any reply body, header or audit row; each provider only ever received its own key.

title: Proxy: provider down then recovers
scenario: Primary has nothing listening; fallback answers. The primary comes up; a call during the 30 s rest; a call after it.
expected: Fallback answers while down and during the rest (primary asked 0 times); after 31 s the primary answers.

title: Proxy: one same-provider retry on 5xx
scenario: Primary returns 500 'error parsing tool call' once, then succeeds; another provider is configured.
expected: HTTP 200 from the primary's second sample; primary asked 2x, the other 0x.

title: Proxy: context too large answered fast
scenario: A ~50k-token request; the lane's providers accept 8k total and 32k input.
expected: HTTP 413 code context_length_exceeded in < 1000 ms; no provider is called.

title: Proxy: too-small provider skipped
scenario: A ~15k-token request; the priority-1 provider holds 8k total, the next 128k.
expected: HTTP 200 from the big provider; small asked 0x; an agent_model_skipped audit names it.

title: Proxy: upstream size refusals give 413
scenario: Both providers refuse for size (413 'Request too large', 400 'maximum context length').
expected: Agent gets 413 context_length_exceeded (not 502); each provider asked exactly once.

title: Proxy: client disconnect mid-stream
scenario: The agent opens a slow streamed call (400 chunks, 20 ms apart) and closes its socket after the first bytes.
expected: The upstream's writes fail within 6 s (the proxy stopped relaying and closed the upstream), and the next call gets HTTP 200.

title: Proxy: owner token never reaches Dahl
scenario: Dahl is public priority 0; the only private provider is down. The owner's private token sends bank/API-key text; a public test token sends a GitHub token.
expected: Owner call fails (502/503) with Dahl asked 0 times; lab call reaches Dahl with the token, API key and card digits absent.

title: Proxy: model preference stays in lane
scenario: The public agent tries to prefer private groq; the owner's agent tries to prefer public Dahl, then private cerebras.
expected: Cross-lane preferences refused (400); cerebras accepted and serves the next call; groq and Dahl get 0 calls.

title: Proxy: non-agent tokens make no model calls
scenario: Dashboard, owner-console, invalid and runner tokens call /v1/chat/completions.
expected: 403, 403, 401, and 403/404; the provider gets 0 requests.

title: Proxy: per-agent rate limit and kill switch
scenario: One agent makes PER_MINUTE+1 calls in a minute, one after a minute, then the kill switch is set.
expected: First PER_MINUTE calls 200, the next 429, after 61 s 200, killed 503 with 0 upstream requests.

title: Proxy: context length advertised per lane
scenario: Private lane has 8k and 131072 providers; public lane only an 8k one. Agents read /v1/models.
expected: Private reports 131072; public reports the 64000 agent minimum.

title: Proxy: 40-message history overhead
scenario: A 40-message conversation (a normal long agent session) through the proxy to an instant mock provider.
expected: HTTP 200 in < 2000 ms total (proxy overhead: scrubbing, sizing, audit).

title: Proxy: 20 parallel calls
scenario: Two agents send 20 concurrent calls to a mock with 50 ms latency.
expected: 20/20 HTTP 200; p95 latency < 1500 ms.

title: Local team routing order
scenario: Requests: python error (rules), percentage (rules), ambiguous with Jev 0.8 'math', Jev 0.4 + router 'code', Jev down + router garbage.
expected: code/rules, math/rules, math/jev, code/router, general/default.

cases: fix this python traceback in my script
help me split the dinner bill fairly
my laptop app keeps freezing on startup

title: RAM guard before loading a local model
scenario: 6 GB free: load general (5.5 GB) and code (1.8 GB); general already loaded at 2 GB free; owner override NEKO_MODEL_RAM_GB_GENERAL=2.
expected: general refused with a message naming 5.5 GB; code ok; loaded ok; override ok.

title: Low RAM: nothing sent to the local model
scenario: psutil reports 3 GB free and no model is loaded; ask_local('general').
expected: TeamError 'Not enough free memory'; 0 model calls.

title: ask_local input limits and reasoning strip
scenario: Empty task, task over MAX_TASK, unknown specialist; then a math answer wrapped in <think>.
expected: Three TeamErrors with 0 model calls; the answer is 'Final: 42' with left_this_pc False.

title: Adviser only through the privacy gateway
scenario: advise() with Dahl's direct URL, the local llama-swap URL, an empty URL and a look-alike path; then the gateway URL.
expected: All four refused with 0 requests; exactly one request, to 127.0.0.1:48950.

title: Adviser use policy in solve()
scenario: use_adviser never; auto with Jev 'direct 0.9'; auto with Jev down; always with an adviser that times out.
expected: 0, 0, 1 adviser calls respectively; the failing adviser gives a local answer with note 'adviser skipped'.

title: Placeholders: Dahl never sees the password
scenario: local_team.advise() through the REAL privacy gateway (detector replaced by redactor.py's cue-word pattern; Presidio not in the image) to a mock Dahl that streams the plan with [PASSWORD_1] split across chunks.
expected: Dahl's request has [PASSWORD_1] and not the password; the returned plan has the real password restored; the caller's key is passed through.

title: Placeholders restored in content and tool calls
scenario: Same password twice in one message, non-streamed; the mock answers using the placeholder in content and a tool-call argument.
expected: Dahl sees [PASSWORD_1] twice (one placeholder per value) and never the value; content and tool arguments come back with the real value.

title: Privacy gateway fallback uses its own key
scenario: Dahl answers 429; the fallback provider has its own key file and model. Two calls.
expected: Both calls answered by the fallback with its own key and model (caller's Dahl key not sent there) and no password; Dahl, which carries the caller's key, is tried first on each call (2x, by design).

title: GPU/VRAM fit of local models on the laptop
scenario: On the owner's laptop (4 GB GPU, 1.2 GB used by apps) llama-swap loads the decider and specialists; measure VRAM spill and tokens/s.
expected: Measured VRAM use and tokens/s per model recorded; no model load pushes free RAM under the 1.5 GB reserve.
